(Side note: I've only done one playthrough of this, so some of the things I've talked about could be different with a different path, but the book should still be interesting on its first read.)
To be quite honest the first Versus book never really caught my attention, but the first book was much shorter and it had lots of world building going on, especially with its political and religious choices. So I figured maybe it needed a first book to get it standing and that the second book would pop, like the Heroes Rise series that I happen to adore.
I was also hoping that the second book would cut back on the political, social, and religious commentary, as they detracted away from the story rather than add to it.
I was INCREDIBLY disappointed to find this book would take that commentary and crank it up to 5000.
Which is sad, because there is bits where the story manages to hold me in, such as during the first trial where we are introduced to some new bright characters who were all very entertaining, and the bits where you actually sit down and talk about Dhanthik are also very interesting.
However the story comes to an absolute stop the moment it decides political commentary is a absolute MUST and it happens so often that it very easily shoves me out of the story and it just makes me roll my eyes and groan loudly. I understand this is what the game wants to try to do but halting the story entirely to ask about your beliefs every few pages is not fun or thought provoking.
The entire 'Make your own planet' subplot was entirely unnecessary, painful, and almost borderline offensive with some of its jabs at religion. I could not bring myself to care about this planet because I felt uncomfortable by the painfully OBVIOUS social commentary it was trying to pull, and halting the story just so you can choose a tax plan and education system is ridiculous. Not to mention the final 'shocker' moment the subplot has was ridiculous.
However, that is my opinion, and I can maybe see how some people may be interested, but overall it took me out of the story completely and it honestly didn't serve any purpose in the story that you would care about.
If you're expecting a bunch of kick♥♥♥♥♥trials where your character goes out and takes names, you're not going to get it from this book. There are bits where you do fight but it is overshadowed by walls and walls of exposition.
On a further note, there's not much character development either, there are certain parts that pay special attention to certain characters, but it left a lot to be desired. It makes me mad because character and story development could easily replace the unnecessary political debates, it's honestly hard to really sit and care for these characters save for a few that do get to show their character.
Not to mention the ending just pads out for pages and pages and it really doesn't feel like much care was put into it as the story switched to telling me the results rather than showing me the outcomes of my choices. Overall it was kinda jarring and almost boring. I may have forgotten some details because of this.
Maybe I'm not smart enough for this, maybe I just don't 'get it'. But when I play a sci fi series like this, choosing tax plans  and deciding if presidential elections are a good thing isn't what I have in mind.
This book WANTS to be deep. It DESPERATELY wants you to think and make connections to this book and real life, but they cram it so far into your face that it just becomes annoying. It becomes blatantly obvious that this book is making commentary on the current state of America and so it makes hard to get back into the book's world. (Side note: Why are you just making commentary on America? Isn't this a vast galaxy that features multiple cultures?)
I'm sad. I WANT to like this book series, I WANT to feel the need to replay it so I can get more endings and features like with the Heroes Rise series, but I just can't bring myself to do it. I had to force myself to finish this. I can only hope the Author improves from this, though I know he can because he can write good book series.
So in my opinion? Unless you're REALLY into political debates with a side of occasional sci-fi plot stuffs. Skip it.

Pretty fun game. Worth the 20$.
Time from Start to Finish (No side Missions): 15-20 hours if you've played videogames before.
Difficulty: 2/5 This game is basically the exact opposite of Dark Souls in terms of difficulty. (Some of the earlier boss fights may be somewhat difficult at first. For one entire playthrough you may die 4 to 5 times. The final boss fight is one of the worst I have ever seen in all the videogames I have ever played. On the flip side, the "Nemesis" system is one of the best "mini-boss" systems I have ever seen. It adds a lot of variety to the game, and I don't think I saw one duplicated boss in 20 hours of playing.)
Fun Scale: 4/5 (Gets reptitive doing the same thing over and over again. The variety of missions aren't very deep. However, incredibly satisfactory to just Hack n' Slash your way through mobs of enemies.
Replay Value: 2/5. Again you're just doing the exact same things over and over as you did when you were playing the main missions. If you're really into Hack n' Slash, then this game is for you.
Variety: 2/5 There isn't much variety of enemies in the game. There's about 9-10 different enemies you'll encounter. However, the variety of "mini-bosses" is extraordinary so this game does make up for its weaknesses somehow. The upgrade system feels like your upgrades really matter and make a huge impact on the game, even for just one upgrade. There are no weapons in this game, you get just the sword, "dagger", and bow which never change in appearance. You can however upgrade them individually. There is no equippable armor but there are skins you can change in the main menu. (One skin adds a sleeve to the default skin!)
Story: 5/5 Very interesting and unique. It kept true with the spirit of the Lord of the Rings while also adding some new depth and texture.
Overall: 3.75/5 (I'm a tough grader, I play a lot of videogames). A lot of this was because of how short the game was. How easy the game was. How pathetic the final boss(es) was. (It's the final boss, it should feel EPIC, but it took less than 20 seconds, I mean.. c'mon.) BUT, the system for the mini-bosses was extraordinary. It was also very well incorporated with free-roaming so you never knew when the next time you'd find another boss around the corner.
Would I recommend this game?
Absolutely. Twenty bucks for twenty hours. Had fun the whole way through despite some glaring flaws. This is a very good game despite how harsh my review was of it. I just want people to know what they're buying.

My favorite zombie game! Its not perfect, it is a bit buggy but the game itself is fantasitc! You have a huge area to explore filled with zombies and places to scavange. This game is all about the survival of your own establisment. You meet new people where you help eatch other out to fight the zombies and to survive in this apozalyptic area. Youll have a main base where you bring all the good you find and you can make upgrades, different purpose rooms etc. You can do alot of stuff that you would actually do in real life if a zombie infestation would happen. You look for supplies, find new, safer homes, outposts and try to find out whats going on. The game plays like a GTA game and handles perfectly so! The fighting, the shooting, the scavenging. its is so damn fun in this game! Everything you do in this game has nice animations, everything from reloading guns, entering a viechle, jumping through windows, making executions on zombies. It is very detailed and it looks amazing! All the loot is randomized so the replayvalue is huge! The loot isnt totally random, everything makes sence, that you will find food at the resturants and guns at the weaponshops e.t.c. I love finding new weapons in this game! It has a huge amount of weapons! The graphics are pretty but it lacks any kind of anti aliasing so its blurry like hell. But you get used to it pretty quick. One really bad thing is that if you start a mission with a teammate, the teammate will run home and after the mission is completed you are all alone. And being alone in this game is not a good idea. It isnt difficult to survive alone if you have a car but if you meet a horde with a mutated super zombie on foot there is a good chance that you will die. In a group up to 3 teammembers its alot safer. Dying isnt just game over either, if you die, you die! You cant reload any past saves or anything so IF you die you will have to control another survivor instead. You will switch around survivor a lot anyways because they will become tired from working. Every survivor has its own talents that you can improve while playing them. There are many little details about each and every survivor like past jobs, skills etc. and that makes it feel alive! Another bad thing is that the missions can be all over the map so you will be driving around back and forth alot but since driving over zombies is fun too it isnt that big of a deal. I really recommend you buying this game!

A beautifully rendered, well written, sweet, funny, and relatable game with an identity crisis.
I'm not one to split hairs about what is and isn't a game. I'm a big tent guy; I welcome all kinds. And the meat of this game, the story and the interactions, is essentially IF. I'm not a huge fan of IF in general, but I would have enjoyed it more if it were presented in that form, boiled down to the dialogue and the (mostly) binary decisions.
And it's a shame, because the developers seem to have a more narrow understanding of what a game needs to be. As such, they threw in action. Jumping puzzles, or jumping tasks, really, and lots of achievement busywork. And the jumping? It screws with the tone without adding much of substance, but more importantly, it screws with the pacing. If this were IF, or even just a story, the pacing would be perfect. Adding a touch of Super Mario isn't an improvement.
Still, this game's got heart. It's laugh-out-loud funny. And it's perfect for anyone who's ever been a little bit of a screw-up, or been friends with one. It's imperfect, but highly recommended.

I'd say it's a good terraria like, I enjoy it a lot. it has crafting, it has mods, hunting, base management, space faring, farming....
However it's not without its small issues :
-some performance issues (I7-2600k + 16GB RAM + GTX760 2GB) when zoomed out in large populated bases. particularly if it's also raining. From more expert players/modders than me, the game seems to be constantly unloading & reloading assets, game needs a better caching system to cut down on the loading/unloading cycles.
-no pause, at all even in single player. a bit annoying though not a huge issue either.
-no keybind for teleportation
-need workshop.... "but dude the game has it ?"  yes it does have it, I mean it NEEDS workshop
-it needs workshop for many quality of life/gaming improvements:
* it's behind terraria in chest/storage management, however a mod fixes that
* most windows are really small: crafting for example shows a handful of items with a lot of screen real estate unused. Again fixable through mods.
* Speaking of windows, those are movable and remembers the position you last put them in, except a bug actually resets those positions every game restart.
-the game has workshop but some stuff is locked from modding specifically new keybinds can't be added for example.
There may be more I forget.
As you can see though it's all pretty minor gripes on an otherwise very nice game if you like the terraria genre.

One of the few gathering games that manages to be fun.
The game includes a diverse amount of biomes and worlds to explore, equipment to find and loot to pillage. Everything is randomized and the experience of travelling through space while returning plunder back to your ship as you gradually build onto it is very satisfying. The game features minor survival elements but is still rather forgiving, and has a simple but fun combat system which gives the player a good feeling of control and precision. Players are even allowed to colonize planets for themselves, and recruit characters to live as tenants or become crew on their ship.
The story mode unfortunately is a rather repetitious chore which rewards players with interesting unique dungeons to raid in turn, and there are imbalances with the loot system which lead to the game rewarding players too much and too easily for plundering neutral settlements instead of spelunking and dungeoneering. Furthermore, if you play the game enough you will begin to see a lack of diversity in the randomization of the worlds, but it is not too noticeable.
Overall, it is one of the only gathering games out there that makes an effort to actually entertain the player instead of just keeping them busy with repetition and pointless baubles.

Being a fan of pinball, I recently bought PW and I am glad I did!
The game runs silky smooth with all eye candy on at 1920x1080 on my i7 6700k, GTX 1080 and 32GB RAM (while this might sound obvious, "Zaccaria Pinball" sometimes manages to stutter slightly with this configuration...).
Among the first things I noticed is the excellent table design and the great game flow as a result of it.
The entire gaming experience just feels natural, the table is easy enough for newbies and challenging enough to satisfy seasoned pinball vets. The table design and the special effects/visuals are just gorgeous, there are many "little things" that show a incedible attention to detail.
All of that puts PW ahead of the competition. I'll put PW on par with "Timeshock" and that means a lot. Yes, there are cheaper tables on the market. However, I strongly prefer one *excellent* table over 5 average ones (I remember "Timeshock" being released in 1997 and it was, IIRC, around 50 bucks. Even today, 20 years later, I play it once in a while, so much about replay value).
As much as I like the table in its current state, there is some room for improvement: regarding the sound effects, "Timeshock" for example, sounds much more natural when the flippers are moving. All sounds and the music could use a little more impactful bass. This contributes a lot to the overall experience. Also, at times, the ball "feels" to light, like it would be hollow. The rubber around the flippers doesn't feel like the real thing, the ball does not bounce off, it behaves as if the flippers would have a sponge wrapped around it, that immediately absorbes the balls impact energy.
Aside from these minor flaws, I can wholeheartedly recommend  "Pinball Wicked" to anyone remotely interested in Pinball! It delivers a great pinball experience with stunning visuals. I wish, the developers would provide a trial version, so everyone could test it out, prior to taking the plunge.

Been watching this one develop for a while and decided to make the plunge and get the early access version (which almost never happens).
First impressions:
Visually: Absolutely gorgeous, I would be hard pressed to find a pinball game that looks this good and polished, definitely in the same league as Pro Pinball Remastered. The rustic looking ball is a nice touch. I play in 1920x1080 with all the eye candy on.
Audibly: Good music and speech, pretty good proportionate mix on volume levels (but customizable). Does have some lapses in music at times but it doesn't bother me enough to knock it.
Gameplay: Not bad at all, could use a little tuning and tweaking but the experience was very enjoyable. Physics are pretty on, but i'd like to see a little more bounce on the flippers (unless this was intended). Ball movement is nice and smooth. Does seem to fly into the outlanes at turbo speed at times but that's kind of what I'm used to with Pinball Arcade. Nudge is about what i would expect it to be.
Control: I use an XBOX 360 wireless controller. No lags whatsoever in the flippers and it's nice and smooth. Flipper power seems a little on the weaker side but it feels pretty good, not too stong like other games. The ability to use both sets of buttons is nice. I prefer the bumper buttons to the triggers myself.
Some observations: Default view was the camera moving with the ball location which was a little bit stuttery. I like a still playfield so one tap of the back button got to me the view i wanted with no camera movement. After that it was very smooth with no lags or hiccups.
My rig is a bit dated and custom built but played this game just fine.
My Specs:
Intel Core i7 3770 @ 3.4 GHz
Asus Sabertooth Z77 Motherboard
16GB RAM (DDR3 - PC3-10700)
eVGA nVidia Geforce GTX 970
Intel 240GB SSD
WD 1TB Velociraptor (10K)
Creative SB X-Fi
LG BD-RE Optical Drive
Corsair Wired Gaming Keyboard/Mouse
2x Dell 1080p Montitors
XBOX Wireless Receiver for PC
XBOX 360 Wireless controller (Chrome)
Overall Opinion: Very well done. Love the theme, all the bells and whistles, music and of course how beautiful it is to look at. Solid gameplay which could use a couple of fine tunings but this was a lot of fun to play. Nice smooth experience with no studders or hiccups (other than camera on mode).
Recommendation: Absolutely. I love pinball and I'll take it any way I can get it. I'm an average player who has been playing for 25+ years. Can't wait to see what these guys come up with next.

It's a good tycoon game about transportation, mostly trains. You also have trucks, trams, buses and trucks, but those are mostly used to set up local networks that enables wider access to your trains,
Train simulation is pretty complex, with lots of factors coming into play: Track curvature, slope steepness, engine power output, tractive power, and weight of the wagons, so a lot of the gameplay is about designing efficient tracks, that allow your trains to navigate through the (fully 3d) terrain in the most efficient way possible; then populating the trains with suitable engines and wagons.
Here I should add that this is unfortunately also the game's weakest point (although it's not such a big deal): laying tracks and modifying terrain is often very quirky. It often takes several tries (and a lot of bulldozing, which also costs you in-game money) to get a track, or junctions, just the way you like it. Crossing rivers and roads is even more complicated, which put me off a bit. All in all, however, while I do think they could have polished this aspect some more, I understand that the complexity of laying tracks is part of the charm of the game, and that how good you are at balancing between length, steepness, curvature and train power will determine how efficient your network will be.
The economic simulation is surprisingly complex, and engaging. Towns will react to your lines by increasing in size and height (sometimes massively). Despite its complexity, it's easy to pick up after reading a couple guidelines given to you at the beginning of the game. I don't think you'd have any trouble with it if you ever played TTD before.
Graphically it is stellar, and once I got my game going, I often found myself just watching how my trains navigate the network I laid out.
Finally, I'll also add that I've owned this game for a few months before reviewing it, and that the devs have adressed many of the issues that the game used to have, and delivered a lot more content with the free USA DLC. In short, if you like trains and tycoon games, this is a good buy.

I want to love this game,but I just cannot. For those of you who are debating about if you want this game or not,read this review,and decide from there. Basically,this games is like a modern day Locomotion or Transport Tycoon,only not as good. Like,at ALL. The game does have redeemable factors,but all the bad things just completely drown them out.
Pros:
-Good Music: I have to say,the music is catchy and is very Tycoon game-ish.
-Decent Graphics: Not the prettiest,but not the most ugly either.
Cons:
-No Objectives:In games like Locomotion,you played on many different maps each with a unique objective (transport a certain amount of goods,reach a certain company rating,etc.) In Train Fever,however,there is no goal in sight other than "Don't go bankrupt!" which is the barebone objective of tycoon games.
-No Rival A.I:No competing companies,no rivals trying to make more money than you,nothing. Just you and yourself,which gets old very fast.
-Bad Construction Tools;Something that should be simple and basic is rather clunky and frustrating. Horrible collision detection (I seriously had collision problems with something that was atleast 50 feet from the track),Landscaping controls that use the camera button to take effect,crossing roads and rails is a pain in the butt,and sooooo much more.
-Poor Performance:Despite the fact that my computer is very modern and runs lots of other games perfectly,Train Fever constantly lags and often takes a few seconds just to do basic things like move the camera.
And finally,the biggest problem of all...
-Crashes,Crashes,and more Crashes:Oh.My.God. This game crashes more than a drunk driver. Gameplay consists of 10 minute sperts before a crash,which deletes your save data if you didn't save before. If the crashes were few and far between,it could be forgivable. But they're not. The longest I've ever gone without a crash was about 10 minutes,and although I went even longer without a crash,the game's perfomance dropped even more,so it looks as though to prevent crashing,the game needs to run badly. And to run well,the game needs to crash constantly. Pick your poison,I say! And not does the game crash a lot,but 9 times out of 10,it's going to not just crash the game,but the computer entirely. This game has crashed on me 8 times,and 4 or 5 of those were hard crashes. Not only that,but it once crashed so hard,the crash error screen crashed too. How the hell do you do that!?
If you haven't figured it out by now,I don;t recommend this game at all. It's way too overpriced for what it is,and even though I got it on sale for $13,it was still too expensive.
Here are 3 better ways to spend that $40:
1.Go buy food,clothes,gas,a gift for your sweetheart,anything really.
2.Buy a bunch of other games on Steam. I recommend the Five Nights at Freddy's trilogy,Team Fortress 2,and Gt Legends,just to name a few.
3.If you stil want your tycoon game fix,buy Locomotion or Rollercoaster Tycoon. Both are timeless classics that still hold up today,and will give you many more hours of enjoyment than this game ever could.

I got the original WMotA game for free during some give away I can't remember. Then one day I looked up and the game was upgraded to the "complete" version for free too. Mind you, I still hadn't even played the game. I looked up some reviews and got a lot of mixed signals about it being good or not so good. The only constant was that it was a "Civ 5" clone. And since I'm a HUGE Civ IV & V fan, I didn't see a point in playing a knock off.
To the point of this review, I made a point of playing this game over the holidays. I didn't want to write a review of it until I played it at least 25 hours and gave it every chance under the sun to impress me. In conclusion, my verdict is...this is an outstanding game!
The first thing I want to say is, this is not some Civ 5 clone. And people saying that have no idea what they're talking about. Just because it has a hex-based tile map seems to give WMotA some stigma of being "like" or "a clone" of Civ5. There are tons of games out with the same system, so that characteristic is more than unfounded to say this game is "like" Civ 5.
In Warlock, you will master economics, amass a versitile army, strategize, and FIGHT! Furthermore, unlike Civ 5, you will not have a DULL moment before pushing the "end turn" button. That's what I hate about all Civ games. You will get to a point where entertainment turns to a chore...and there's nothing you can do about it.
And unlike Civ games, each turn in WMotA matters! You not only get to pick what building you want to build for what city, but where to place them in your region. That's part of the fun in the city-building aspect. Each tile may give a specific bonus and it's worth checking out what gets placed where. It's worth checking out if you have a resource in your region you can exploit. In Civ games, you just worry about the percentages despite its land resources. In WMotA, you can research spells to change the dynamics of the tile...which in essence, changes the percentages or bonuses of that tile. And there are a ton of spells to do a ton of different things. Too many in fact to go into. But volcano spells and removing swamps to make fertile terrain is pretty epic in this game. You'll see when YOU play.
But what I like most about WMotA is its variety. Look folks, you will never amass the amount of different units you can...collect...in this game and even remotely compare it to Civ 5. I mean (laughing histerically) this is supposed to be a fantasy game, right? But you got armored soldiers from a Civ game; you've got fantasy units from an Age of Wonders game; you've got undead units from a Lords of the Ring game; you've got blood sucking units from a Van Helsing game; you've got badass bears of all types from every game...I mean...LOL...it's ridiculous. And here's the kicker: No land-based melee unit can attack a flying range unit. So you won't see a knight on a horse killing a blackhawk helicopter like you WILL see in a Civ game! In WMotA, these units serve purposes true to logical gameplay. Not just some random point system statistical outcome.
And then there are the portals that send you to other worlds. Where the hell is that in a Civ 5 game? In Civ 5 you play on 1 map; O-N-E!  WMotA has the main map, and then there are portals that can send you to as many other maps as you request in the game setup. Listen folks, I selected the XL map (the largest) with six alternate worlds (the most) against eight other mages (the highest) on the difficult setting (the default). It was a mad house... A MAD HOUSE! I had no idea I had to fight monsters and rouge civilizations along WITH the others mages in the game. Everybody was fighting everybody. It was insane! It was wonderful!!
In fact, the only, and I do mean only, downside to the game was its diplomacy aspect. It truly sucks. I can't even begin to lie about that; especially when compared with Civ games. I guarantee (unless you're a lousy player) that any "demand" from the enemy AI given to you will result in WAR. You're not even going to consider the ridiculous stuff this game offers you to keep from going to war. The other stuff though is plausable and makes the game fly by unscathed.
But back to the portals, man. They occasionally send up these strong monster units, and if you aren't ready for them, they will wreck havoc. Then there are the quest (again, nothing like Civ 5) that sometimes make you defeat enemies you've never even heard of, man. Like the time the game dropped this♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off supernatural ghost smack down on my settlement without a hero in sight. That green ghost...man...he laid a smack down on my candy♥♥♥♥♥like The Rock. I finally got my hero chick over there to battle it. They fought for five turns until she finally overcame him and I won the quest. Got some sweet rewards too. Yet, that was only a SMIDGEN of what was going on with my other endeavours during those turns.
So I got pretty confident in my efforts and decided to send my tanked-out Hero Knight into one of these portals. When the map switched over...LOL...I was SURROUNDED by doubled-headed dragons, Fire Elementals, and other high-powered monsters I can't even name. I could not believe what quick work they made of my Rambo-Lancelot. I was truly butt-hurt after that encounter. I called the game a cheater and hurled all sorts of foul insults at the monitor for hours before quitting for the night. Heck, I almost quit the game twice after that beatdown.
But guess what? The next day and several hours later, I researched a spell that would bring my hero back to life. Not only did I finally get him back, but he was still tanked-out. I love this game. The next time, I sent a few zomie units to another portal to check THAT world out. Of course it looked TOTALLY different. Nice diversity in the maps here! My zombies didn't last long either but the spolied sacks of meat had like 60 hit points apiece. They lasted longer than the Hero Knight did. P.S., did I tell you one of my zombies was walking around on fire...after getting blazed by that two-headed dragon?
BUGS: Believe it or not, there aren't many bugs in this game. In fact, I really searched and only found 1; and it isn't even that major. What happens is you sometimes get double event screens but you're only able to see the last event. So you can't close the first event or see it for that matter. You have to hit the escape key which takes you to the main menu. Select "resume" and you're back to your game and are able to close the last event screen. It's not as bad nor annoying as it sounds once you understand what's happening. It also doesn't happen that often. You can see what you missed at the top of the menu bar where the quests are kept.
I know this was long (much longer than I meant it to be) but I wanted to express my disagreement with some of the claims out there. This is no Civ 5 clone. It's a great turn-based/action/strategy/4x game that fixes a ton of stuff that Civ games and Endless Legend gets wrong. You can hire heroes and equip them with armor, weapons and artifacts much like Endless Legend & Fallen Enchantress - Legendary Heroes.
In conclusion, thank you for reading my review. This is my opinion showing no bias for nor against other reviews or reviewers but solely based on my gameplay experiences. In final, this game's sole similarity to Civ 5 is its hex-based tiles. With that in mind, I found WMotA to be a Civ 5/Endless Legend/Fallen Enchantress - Legendary Heroes chimera. And it would be WELL WORTH your time to experience it at least once for yourself. Thank you for your time. GO PLAY SOMETHING!

Long Live the Queen has been a pleasant surprise to me. I had somewhat moderate expectations for this game and I was blown away by it.
This game can be very challenging on the first playthrough (I know I'm not the only one who came to a dead end and had to start over), but once you get to know the major events that will unfold and you prepare yourself accordingly, you'll manage to survive long enough to reach the end of the game, typically on your second playthrough.
But that's not the end of it. I'll dare say that's where the real fun starts. Just by beating the game once or twice you'll barely scratch the surface of this game. You'll realize that there's much more to see because you'll be missing tons of achievements, epilogues, and deaths (yes, even "collecting" diferent kinds of deaths can be fun and a real challenge). You'll start wondering what will happen if you focus on learning different skills and how the storyline will change if you do. What if I become a military genius? Should I embrace the power of Lumen? If I'm a ruler, I should improve my social skills, so what will happen if I do? This kind of questions will surely arise if you have enjoyed the gameplay, and they'll make you start over and over just to satisfy your curiosity and further enjoy the game. So if you get hooked as much as I did, you can easily pass the 20h mark and still have things to try and achievements to unlock.
Still, it's not a game for everyone, but if you don't mind (or even enjoy, as I have to admit I do) the cutesy artstyle, you can bear with some repetition (there's a skip button thankfully), and you appreciate games where your choices really matter, you'll probably have an enjoyable time with it.

I really really want to give this game a positive review....but I just can't. I bought this game last year in February so I witnessed the course of development it took the last months. I have waited since then to write a (positive) review because I think this game has a great potential and when I bought it last year it already had a solid and fun base for an EA game.
What it lacked back then was the longterm motivation. Once you had your basic food and water supplies there was no more need for exploration. All Island were basically the same, a shipwreck here and there but that was it. So I was very very escited for new content. Because the game is developed by only a small team (2 guys if I remember correctly?) updates take some time to be released. But this is where the downfall began...instead of introducing new content to make the game more of a challenge they implemented.....Seaforts! What? Yeah right, Seaforts. The things build by the British in WW2 in the North Sea (!). Other than being totally out of place they provide an additional loot spawn for things you can also find in ship wrecks. Since then (over a year ago now) there hasn't changed much about the amount of content that was released...
To be fair, the developers did a great job updating the engine (e.g. new crafting system - some like the old one better but it's okay) and improving the visuals. For an indie EA game Stranded Deep has stunning and very impressive graphics creating a fantastic atmosphere. Sitting at you campfire at night starring up in the night sky...thats just beautiful ..but that only makes the lack of content more frustrating because I really want to play this game.
So to sum it up: I think the developers are too focused on details instead of expanding the core of the game itself. Wildboars, snakes, tools etc. ... that is all nice to have but once you managed the start the game is basically over. Exploring the ocean and other island...pff, why take a risk when I can sit comfortably in my house once it is build?
This game needs to take a step forward on the macrolevel, not on the microlevel!
I will gladly change this review to a positive one once this happens, until then buy it at your own risk. You might be disappointed after a short time.

At the time of writing, this game is in early access on Steam.
I find this game really interesting. It is a nice appraoch to survival and crafting, and I don't think there's anything out there like this at the moment. That can be a pro and con, however. Take a second to imagine how much you can do on a deserted island - okay, got it? That's how much you can do in the game. Crafting is very basic at the moment, and that helps the learning curve stay fairly low. I don't think that is an issue, but some gamers who want a very in depth crafting and exploration game may have a problem with that. This of course is mostly at fault due to the stage of game development. They have items and areas ready for new features in the game, so more will come. I'm sure there will be more environmental hazards as development continues as well.
Personally, I see this game as a relaxing alternative to your typical "raid or be raided" mentality, and you only have to worry about starvation/thirst and sharks for the most part. So don't take this game too seriously. Focus on storing your vital supplies like food, water and wood, and then start building a house. Build several houses. It doesn't matter. Maybe in the future, storms could sweep things back out to sea (and possibly re-plant them as loot later on), but right now that's not a worry. Build some insane mansion and then do it somewhere else. The end game is just what you make it here, so make it exciting! Hunt a shark, build a raft and try to ramp it off something else, try to ride a whale, or furnish a house!
The best part is, when you least expect it, you'll catch that poisonous fish because it's just begging to get hit with a spear, and then BAM. Where's your antibiotics? You don't have any? Oh... well uh, you're dead now.
I won't comment any more on what I expect from this game or how I see it going through development. It's a trend now to release early access to Steam, and it does benefit bug testing and game development, but at the same time plenty of games take the money and put it somewhere else in their company. So I won't even begin to speculate on something that's so far from done.

This game has a heck of a reputation for being difficult.  Seems like any list of hardest games ever includes Dark Souls. I half expected to rage quit this game inside of a few hours, mainly because my gaming skills have never been that great.
So I dove in expecting to get whupped.  Whupped I got.  Regularly.  I also found one of the best games I've ever played.  It is instantly engaging and I'm transported into the world of Lordran.  The world design is beautiful and clever, areas interconnect in surprising ways, and you'll spot places you've visited while enjoying a scenic vista from a high point.  The world really comes alive for me with a bleakness and sadness that isn't accidental.
The game does not hold your hand like many modern games do.  I'm often left wondering where to go next, or faced with multiple choices and only the difficulty of the denizens are clue to my next path.
The game IS difficult, however it's not the type of difficult that requires lightning reflexes (although they'd help).  Analyzing your failures leads to improvement.  The penalty for death isn't too harsh.  You return to the last bonfire (checkpoint).  You lose any souls  (experience & currency) you hadn't spent.  All the monsters you've killed respawn.  You can recover your souls if you make it back and pick them up without dying again, which usually isn't a problem.
If you stick with it, you'll reach a point where something clicks, and the mechanics of the game make sense.  It doesn't get easy, but it gets much easier.
Bosses are another matter.  They are supremely challenging and incredibly varied.  They don't feel cheezy in difficulty.  There always seems to be a way to figure them out and put the hurt on them.  Adapt and conquer.
Multiplayer can be your focus, or it can be almost completely ignored, and it does it with grace.  You can try to summon help or offer yourself to help others.  You can also invade other players, or be invaded.  Being informed that you've been invaded while working your way to a boss is guaranteed to get your blood pumping.
All in all I'm loving Dark Souls, and can't wait to get back to it.

A beautifully rendered, well written, sweet, funny, and relatable game with an identity crisis.
I'm not one to split hairs about what is and isn't a game. I'm a big tent guy; I welcome all kinds. And the meat of this game, the story and the interactions, is essentially IF. I'm not a huge fan of IF in general, but I would have enjoyed it more if it were presented in that form, boiled down to the dialogue and the (mostly) binary decisions.
And it's a shame, because the developers seem to have a more narrow understanding of what a game needs to be. As such, they threw in action. Jumping puzzles, or jumping tasks, really, and lots of achievement busywork. And the jumping? It screws with the tone without adding much of substance, but more importantly, it screws with the pacing. If this were IF, or even just a story, the pacing would be perfect. Adding a touch of Super Mario isn't an improvement.
Still, this game's got heart. It's laugh-out-loud funny. And it's perfect for anyone who's ever been a little bit of a screw-up, or been friends with one. It's imperfect, but highly recommended.

So I have barely played any Ultra Street Fighter IV ever.... Well on Steam it looks that way, but I had it for Windows Live which is why my achievement list looks odd as it says I got the clear 10 trials and clear all trials with one character at the same time. I also main the game on Playstation 4 now and already had it on PS3 and Xbox 360. So I have a little experience with this game before hand.
With that said I have noticed some odd things about this particular version. Like hitting an opponent with an anti-air and then getting hit by said opponent from the ground in the very next frame. All of the other frames disappeared. I have it set to run at a fixed rate as my computer can run the game way faster than necessary. So that should not have happened, but it did.
The other thing I noticed is the game sometimes has button lag in this version, but not always. It is very inconsistent about that. So that is also kind of interesting to note.
Other than those issues this game is fantastic. Despite how some people complain and say, "Well I am still waiting for the Ultra Street Fighter IV Hyper Rainbow Edition", these add-ons were actually heavily demanded by the hardcore fanbase that have supported it through each version. Very few games and especially fighting games will ever have the longevity that Street Fighter IV has had and still has now.
With Street Fighter V's beta fast approaching and that game already looks like it might be the successor that one would hope for after a title like Street Fighter IV, there is no better time than now to join into a game that has such a massive community and is both good for casuals and hardcore players. I will warn you that if you are fairly new, you might want to go into challenge mode and try some of the trials to learn a few basics before getting online as experienced players might hand you a bit of a whooping, but it is deffinitly a game that will forever be remembered.
Street Fighter rarely disappoints and we have seen many great titles come out of the series. Ultra Street Fighter IV is a testement to how great the series can be and it also raised the standard for fighting games which is why many others since then have had trouble as they get seen as a bit of a side note, but I have played most of those as well. I highly recommend this title for old veterans of fighting games like myself to the newest of new interested in just trying one out. Either way you are likely to have fun.

El estudio independiente Jamit Games trae a la mesa una propuesta divertida y llena de acción: Jump Stars, donde con risas, disparates y ratos hilarantes para disfrutar con nuestros amigos desde la comodidad del sillón.  Dentro de Jump Stars hallamos variedad de minijuegos donde el único nos toca enfrentarnos al resto de personajes (no se pueden usar NPC’s) e intentar obtener la mayor cantidad de puntos.
Los minijuegos en Jump Stars son super sencillos, no tienen mecánicas complicadas ni métodos difíciles para salir victoriosos, lo que asegura la diversión total tanto para grandes como para chicos. Cualquier jugador sin importar su nivel de experiencia podrá jugar sin problemas y acostumbrarse a los controles , pues son muy sencillos: brinca, golpea, y muévete.
La falta de posibilidades para enfrentarnos a la IA deja mucho que desear, pues probablemente la mayoría del tiempo no tengamos la facilidad de contar con otros 3 amigos para crear una buena contienda, y la falta de personajes controlados por la IA vuelve el juego algo poco emocionante y sin ese sabor de restregarle a otros en la cara tus victorias.
En Jump Stars -según su argumento, somos participantes de un concurso de televisión, junto con un presentador tan loco como el show que presenta, donde somos los ‘favorecidos’ a ser concursantes. Los personajes son solo cubos, muy chistosos,  a los cuales podemos cambiar su apariencia con una cantidad moderada de posibilidades estéticas.
Técnicamente el juego anda muy bien, sin problemas en los FPS o bugs. En cuanto al sonido es bastante bueno, tan acorde con las circunstancias de juego que hará las partidas aun más graciosas y llenas de locuras. de hecho, el audio del juego logra crear ese ambiente de programa de telivisión y fiesta del que trata su pequeña trama. Pasaremos muchos momentos de carcajadas a causa de ‘sana’ competición, y en muchas ocasiones porque los jugadores tratarán de hacer que sus enemigos caigan en situaciones incómodas con tal de obtener la mayor puntuación. Las voces se encuentran en inglés, todos los textos llegan perfectamente traducidos a Español.
Lo malo del juego es la poca variedad de minijuegos, y aunque son muy cómicos, se vuelven repetidos muy pronto, haciendo que el título se pueda tornar algo aburrido tras un tiempo jugándole. Al menos, esto se compensa con la contienda que habrá entre los mismos jugadores, donde los amigos se verán en disputas con sus camaradas para ver quien logra salir victorioso, y no hay mejor guerra contra la monotonía que hacerle un ‘en tu cara’ a tu mejor amigo.
Es innegable que Jump Stars es un juego muy gracioso y apto para todos los públicos, donde sin duda alguna los jugadores pasaran ratos de entretenidos -y uno que otro ragequit quienes son más competitivos. Por otro lado, recalcamos que la diversión es mayor entre más jugadores hayan en partida, pues cuando solamente juegan dos personas, todo parece aburrido.
Jump Stars ofrece un multijugador que nos recuerda a Mario Party o Crash Bash, y con un poco más de contenido que haga más variado sus mini-juegos, todo sería fantástico. El juego está disponible para PC, Xbox One y PlayStation 4.

OK. So I have over 600 hours of my life invested in Miscreated. Am I happy with the game? Yes. For the most part. The game has its glitches and certain things do not work flawlessly. That is to be expected of a game still in Beta. Read the disclaimer. It's not like they are hiding the fact that the game is not complete. Every game has its challenges for the devs. Sometimes I get upset when the game crashes at an inconvenient time. Sometimes it is due to my computer. Sometimes it is the server crashing. The good thing is that when you restart the game and spawn back in, you are not bombarded by the mutants when you spawn. Usually you can get right back into your vehicle and keep going with whatever you were doing. Not a HUGE problem like most people complain about.
I have played on private and public servers. Everybody that I run across in the game seems pretty happy with the game. Each person playing has a totally different experience. Some people like the PVP aspect of the game. Some like PVE. You can figure out what is best for your liking and play the way you want to. If you like PVP, you can pretty much go into any public server and start looking for a gun to shoot, while being shot at from other players. It can be very exciting trying to survive. Alot of people like this play style. It definately makes it harder to play.
On the other hand, if you like PVE, it is very good as well. You could join a clan that already has a private server OR you could support the devs by renting a server for about $35 US dollars a month. Don't be discouraged by the people complaining about the price. The devs have to make a paycheck to keep developing the game. There is nothiong unfair about that at all. Would you pay less than $1.50 a day to play a good game? It is well worth it in my opinion. If you go back and look at all the updates that have been made you will see that the devs are working hard to try to make this a groindbreaking game. Look at all the similar games coming out.I have not played many of them but I read the discussions.  They have their problems too.
Should you buy Miscreated? Absolutely. You will enjoy this game if you like this type of game.
I would say, buy it, try it, find a good server. Figure out your favorite playstyle (PVP Vs. PVE). Search, shoot, build, explore. Whatever you want.
Make sure you check the specs to run the game before you buy it. There is a webpage that is easy to find called "can I run Miscreated" and you can check your specs before buying. I was able to run the game with my onboard graphics. It was under the suggested specs and it still ran. Low FPS but was still able to play.
Buy it. Try it. Two thumbs up from me.

I came into this wanting a train game where I could set up routes and make money to get new trains and routes, just a basic train tycoon sort of experience. That's pretty much what this game offers, but only at a very shallow level. I'm sad to say it didn't live up to my expectations at all.
As a train set it is extremely limited in what you can do and requires extensive time to unlock any eras or vehicles at all to play with. There is no competitive element. So, just what is compelling here?
Most of it felt to me very incomplete and broken, with very poor feedback on what systems are doing under the hood and therefore little way to make sense of its failings. Often things just won't work for no reason. It's hard for me to rationalize why this game can't measure up in a fairly dead / abandoned genre, as it seems to have plenty of good ideas and then nothing at all to hold them together. If this were an early access alpha I would call it promising.
Instead I'm surprised that this game came out last year and it still hasn't been patched so that track and road laying were not so cumbersome, limited, and fails so often. I can't think of any problems mentioned in Rock Paper Shotgun's review that have actually been taken care of, and it's been a long time and many patches since so just what is happening here where a game is released with serious, unintentional flaws and just keeps them?
You'd be better off with Sid Meier's Railroads! or for a single-player transport tycoon experience maybe Cities in Motion 2. This game just feels extremely unfinished and I feel really betrayed that they made me pay 35$ for it. You'd think a 65% user rating would mean something but the rating system has really failed here. I don't know what people are expecting, thign thing is probably way better than Cities XXL and some shovelware tycoon game, but compare it to games that came out in 2006 and it's a real disappointment.

This game is frustrating beyond belief! I was a hardcore OpenTTD and CIM2 & 1 player and managed to achieve massive and functional cities but this?! This thing right here is just plainly stupid. It tries to wow you with nice graphics and at first you might fall for how great it looks but you just wait for this bug fest! Btw. this is my first ever hate comment and first game ever to make me so angry. I really tried to overcome countless amount of problems but it's just impossible.
First of all UI is just terrible. Windows can't be resized, they pop up in random places (sometimes beyond your screen), buttons are tiny, everything requires loads clicking especially if you manage to grow your corporation to a decent size. Developers recently added auto renew option to your lines. Great. It doesn't change the fact that you still have to manually click on every line and chose which car/train you want to use as your new vehicle. What if a new model is researched? Well, repeat that whole process. Is it really that difficult to think and allow to select many lines rather than just one and make batch changes to them?
Other UI problems include little things like the fact that when changing a name of your line you have to always press and hold backspace to delete a default "line 1" name. You can't select what you've written, you can't copy it, you can't move your cursor. Basically you can't do anything that Notepad application can. Little things but wait until you have 100s lines and want to do some simple cleanup.
Bigger errors include things like a lack of save menu! I mean this is just ridiculous. When saving you have to type your name and that's it. You can't select a previous save so if you make one spelling mistake you will create a new save file or what's worse you can easily ovewrite a different game. You can't load a game from any other screen but main menu and all auto save files are mixed with your regular ones so it's just a massive cluster ♥♥♥♥.
Enough about a terrible UX. How about the game itself? I said already that it looks great but that's about it. There is absolutely no AI. ZERO! Your vehicles will move along set paths and that's it. It doesn't matter that there might be other vehicles blocking it, if it's stuck it will be stuck forever and you won't know because obviously there is nothing that would inform you.
Your trains will always stop on the same platforms. There is no point in building big train stations because computer will always use the same place to load and unload which is totally ridiculous as there might be 5 billion trains waiting in line to one platform while there are 7 other available. You might think that maybe I need to build signals? I tried. I really tried but this game only has 2 and all they do is let or stop a train. They won't direct to a different track, they won't do anything useful. You need to have them so your silly train drivers won't crash into one another but you can't use them for anything useful. Just bloody terrible!
Building roads and tracks is just totally unbelievably idiotic. Route finder will prefer to build massive, stupidly high bridges or long tunnels and claim that it's cheaper that just laying a road on a hill. You also have to lay paths in separate segments and seems like height is applied to a whole section so you end up with these ridiculous lines that costs a fortune and totally wrecks surroundings because computer seems to mix uber high bridges with total destruction of nature. Same with depots and other structures (not that there is many of them). If you put one down on a slight hill, you won't get a gradual terrain alignment, you'll get a fricking cliff in the middle of a city that looks weird as hell.
But the worst of it all is cargo. First of all there are only 4 types which you can increase with mods but that doesn't change the fact that factories doesn't follow any rules at all. They sometimes won't produce anything while suggesting that you can increase manufacture by shipping more of the produce. How am I supposed to increase sending of ZERO??!! Then they'll say that line is in no use even if city is accepting resources and all of them are properly connected.
That's actually another thing. There is no explanation to how all of these things work. No tutorial no nothing. If there was a wiki made by developers that would in depth describe the engine of this game maybe you could understand why certain things are happening but at this point it's just a massive lottery. Loads people are speculating on the internet and share their experiments but no one knows for sure. For example there is apparently a 20 minutes limit on waiting time for a cargo to be picked up but I only know this from players that observed such behavior.
You don't know how population is transferring, you don't know why cargo is not moving, you don't have any proper stats, there are no good overlays, you can't even set your trains and truck to unload outside their dedicated destination (like a transfer station), performance is ridiculous even on high spec computers and more and more issues.
Seriously, this game is more like an Alpha then anything else. It's not even about bugs which there is plenty but about the whole way this game works. How in 2015, can you make a product that is waaaaay worse than Railroad Tycoon 2 that was launched 17 years ago!!! It really annoys me that Steam is letting things like this go. Is there zero quality control?
+ Graphics are pretty nice but ruined by things like ghost buses and horse carts, people waiting on bus stations in a perfectly aligned grid and disappearing if there is too many of them and of course trains and buses reversing in place.
- everything above.
This game has a great potential but god dammit there is still a lot to do. Shouldn't be released by any standards.

It's a good game, but it has a few issues. (free of spoilers)
1) Storyline interference from regular gameplay.
2) No local saves make choices TOO permanent.
3) Story seems to go from slow to over.
4) It definitely has upsides if you enjoy killing zombies like Raid kills roaches...
1) One big problem with this game is that they keep sending you on missions to find/help/bail out people from your survivor group while you should be doing storyline missions. This causes a problem in certain parts because people can be killed if you don't bail them out, but your storyline could be affected as well. I get that this is what adds a bit of realism and difficulty to the game, but on my first time through, I didn't know this, and had to start over after about 8 hours of gameplay!!!
2) Oh, and the reason I had to start over is due to cloud-based game saves. There is very little experimentation you can do with your characters and story unless you plan to play through at least a second time. If your main character dies, oh well. They stick you with one of the other survivors. If you want to try guns for awhile and think that a specialization might help, but find out you hate it, oh well! It just makes the game a bit more frustrating, because you can get overrun in a heartbeat if you aren't 100% focused on every detail when you play. Oh, and don't stay away for too long or your group can all get sick and die!
3) There is a chance it was the way I played through it. I just know that you have to meet up with a group of survivors. You have to nurture them, because you become their leader in a matter of, well you just are. When you first start, you only have a couple people, so at some point you might have to stop if everyone is tired or hurt. Later. if you're good at swapping back and forth when they do get hurt or tired and use them all to round characters out, you take them from being a rag-tag bunch of malcontents to a well oiled machine in nothing flat. Now the problem with this is that you start getting to the point of efficiency. This means you can run around and collects supplies WHILE doing story mission. So when you get to this point you start blowing through missions like they didn't even affect you. And next thing you know, you're doing 4 story missions in an hour and well... Done. Sure, that's where DLC comes in, but I told myself "oh, lets do one more mission." And the game said "here's your final mission." At least I was right.
4) However, they have roaming zombie hoards wandering the streets. Hotwire the nearest car and run them down! Need to take out frustrations? Baseball bat to the zombieskull works wonders! Oh, and when you finally get far enough to get an assault rifle? DONE. Sure you can break weapons and cars, and run out of ammo for guns... But then you just go wander and raid for some more and start the zombiecide all over again!

This game preface, idea, and game play is all cool. What can be uncool though is when you lose a character and you've invested so much time in them, you begin wondering how to turn off the auto save. Just a heads up before I start I couldn't believe when I was playing that this game isn't multiplayer - and that the idea of working with other people (or friends) would be awesome. I repeat : THIS GAME IS NOT MULTIPLAYER.
Does that mean don't play it? Depends...
The story goes you are a man who stumbled into town and upon exploring you find a church full of survivors. A bit later into the story, you hear the military has also set up an outpost in the town but on the other side. You go see them, and you find out that they really couldn't care less, and that they recommend you leave immediately.
The gameplay itself is pretty good - consisting of a 3rd person view and being capable to control more than 1 character... but you can only control one at a time. You can tell other characters to follow you and assist you or you can tell them to come search a location that you've cleared. There are times though where you are faced against this giant zombie boss and all you have is two bullets and a broken machete hoping to take this guy out (so FYI if you hate a bit of grinding in games you may dislike this). The repairing can become a nuisance, but building repair shops or first aid centers (of a few things that you can do) add a bit of depth to the game and really make it feel like it's yours. Another cool feature is when you clear out zombies you are able to set up another "home-base". Cars, weapons, items and so forth are found while you free-roam the map. Look-out points can be discovered and climbed which makes identifying what's in the surrounding environment a little easier.
I like this game, I would like it even more if it had multiplayer. I enjoy playing it but some would put it as a time killer. Either way though if your looking for an open world zombie game this may be for you.

As an avid fan of Tolkien's work, I was worried that
, with its flashy screenshots, would introduce flashy magic or similar stuff too much apart from the lore.
I was happy to find that concern nil: while they have certainly taken many artistic liberties and little inaccuracies abound, the overall lore is adeptly executed.
Here I will cover both the main game and briefly its expansions.
You play as Talion, a ranger and a great warrior. He and his family get murdered by orcs, but a vengeful wraith brings him back, effectively rendering him immortal. Together they start a reign of terror in Mordor to murder all the orcs.
You have several objectives:
Conveniently, the curse of the wraith keeps you from leaving Mordor giving an in-universe reason for the boundary. Otherwise, a large region of Mordor is up for exploration. Everything is accessible from the beginning, though you get more skills and upgrade weapons along the way.
Wraith grants you The Sight, that's basically an X-ray vision with Terminator-grade recognition powers to identify mission objects and special enemies from afar, hidden stashes from up close.
Missions, while usually occurring within the same open-world region, are found around the map launching a separate mission phase, whereupon you must focus on the mission lest it get cancelled or utterly failed (with endless re-dos) by useless wandering or loitering.
Missions are reasonably varied, though aside from the few rescue missions, they very often involve massacring or assassinating countless orcs. It's cool that many quests can be completed either through direct combat or by more tactical stealth strikes.
I played exclusively with keyboard+mouse combo but gamepad should work alright.
Moving Talion works well and expectedly: mouse moves camera, WASD moves Talion. Aside from running, you can stalk, climb almost any surface and use ropelines to swing long distances.
Combat is of the safe formula: attacks, combos and parries work with a couple of buttons. However, the controls soon get much more complex: there's a separate key for each special combat ability to a total of some ten different keys. That's huge for a mere action-adventure.
Granted, not all of them are needed all the time but it makes it hard to return to the game after a long break.
Completing quests and generally wreaking havoc awards exp that yields various skills and upgrades to make your un-life easier. These range from e.g. pinning orcs with arrows to tele-strikes to insta-kills (many involving those extra buttons), among others.
It's particularly fun to get to tame and ride the crazy monster animals of Mordor, like warg-like caragors and troll-like graugs. Especially graugs are super-fun as they both barf and munch on the silly Uruks.
All regular enemies are orcs of different kinds: warriors, archers, berserkers etc. and have their special skills. Any of them can be promoted to captains, receiving a name, quotes and special abilities (and/or weaknesses).
Because of special abilities, captains are usually harder to kill than normal orcs: you might even need to beat a short QTE to finish them.
Captains hang around doing orc-things: organizing hunting parties, hosting drinking feasts, trying to assassinate each other, you know, the normal stuff that bigwigs-in-chief do. The thing is, you can infiltrate any of these and ruin their day. The reward for captain skin is a shiny rune to upgrade your weapons, the worse the enemy the better the rune.
If they still manage to slay you, they become your Nemesis, which is infuriating so of course you try to kill them again. A kind of multiplayer feature, you may encounter the Nemesis of your friends and avenge them too.
As a late-game feature, it's possible or even necessary to build an army of your own by converting the orcs and their dear leaders to your cause by mind tricks.
I completed the main game to 100% in 28 hours. But it got two big expansions, both of which introduced their own maps with new game mechanics.
brings a new biome to bring some color to the greyscale of Mordor. It introduces new creatures (similar to previous caragors and graugs), along with a new friendly face involving a story to hunt those creatures.
has you play the wraith. He works a bit differently to Talion and has some awesome special powers but the story felt more lackluster, probably because it has so little to do with Tolkien's original lore.
The rest of the DLCs are mainly cosmetic. The Test challenges introduce leaderboards with specific challenges that really test your skills with the game mechanics. You have to play at least a couple of them for all achievements.
Very stable and awesome graphics. Not even the few QTEs in combat bring too much shame to it. I had fully completed it achievement-wise after 54 hours, so I dare claim it has plenty of content too.
Combined with lots of (in Tolkien-terms) fitting lore, I think
is a must-play action-adventure for any avid gamer.

Absolutley love this game, gives you a challenge of surviving and living off the land.

Negatives
-Mae is the worst and most unlikeable protagonist I have ever been forced to play as. She constantly ruins her friends lives and never faces consequences for her idiotic actions. She also is terrible to her family, both indirectly and directly, even though they only want to support her.
-The plot of the game is horrible. Nothing happens and all the interesting plot points are dropped or never mentioned again.  The ending is also atrocious and anticlimactic.
-The platforming elements are ruined by floaty controls. Your character slides and glides on surfaces like she's on ice. Also some jumps are near impossible with how the interactable environments blend with the background.
-All the minigames are boring and pointless with ugly visuals and animations with the exception of the computer game you can play which is more engaging and fun than the main game.
-All the characters are shallow and boring with the exception of Bea, which is debateable. Greg is funny for a minute before becoming useless and annoying. Angus is boring and the game expecting you to put time into getting to know him is insulting. All the side characters are meaningless and serve to push either the creator's politics or pad out the game to make it appear deeper than it is.
-Did I mention the politics? This game has a lot in it and if you came for a fun "horror" experience be prepared to sit through some lectures before you get to do anything fun.
-The dream secquences are boring after the first one, and serve no purpose. Like, there is actually no point to them? Besides maybe the final twist? But really they are useless opportunities to push the visuals.
-The soundtrack is the same price as the game if you purchase all the parts.
Positives
+The art style is very good with the exception of some minigames. Other than that the game is very beautiful and fun to look at.
+The computer game you can play is very fun and well made.
+The music is very good, fitting the tone of each scene perfectly.

"Long Live The Queen" feels quite literally like a double-edged sword as a game. On your first playthrough, it is a gambling game. You have no idea what to do, how to spend your points wisely, and who wants to kill you. Hilariously this works together with the plot when you realize that you are playing as a 14 year old girl who has just been given immense power over an entire kingdom. You will most certainly die at some point and the game knows it (There are even achievments to motivate you to discover all the ways you can die). Thankfully, the game autosaves every few minutes and in separate save files so you can choose how far back you want to go. The enjoyment of the game comes from leveling up skills and discovering how the story unfolds because of what you learned. At first, your main goal is just to survive to see the credits. However, the game provides a surprising amount of hidden story bits that merit multiple playthroughs. Now that you are familiar with the skills, mood cycle, and time management, the game becomes more strategic. There is an undeniable satisfaction to be had when you achieve that perfect ending. At the same time, thanks to the game's humor, it is just as entertaining to fail as it is to succeed.

Highly fun, highly frustrating and very addictive Long Live the Queen is a wonderful introduction to the Visual Novel genre and the perfect game for anyone who's ever wanted some Game of Thrones in their Magical Girl Anime.

One of the few visual novels on which I've spent more than 2~3 hours in one session.. It's a great example that sets itself apart from the stereotype understanding of the term/genre, visual novel. Most people would probably expect walls of texts with mediocre choice transitions and though being a VN it still consists of mainly reading, you'll find yourself doing a bit more than just that.
You will be levelling skills to progress through a branched out story making choices as the 'to-be Queen' week by week. Levelling these skills can be heavily reliant on your mood which you can regulate by taking part in activities, events or making certain choices. The order and acquisition rate at which you get certain skills will affect the choices you will be able to make, so each playthrough is sure to be different. The dialogue is just right in that it doesn't drag on, stays on topic and keeps you focused on what's to come and the tasks ahead of you without losing it's pace. This combination that keeps you reading, thinking, making choices and planning your weekly activities really makes you feel as if you're controlling the story rather than just reading it out of a book.
As usual, there's your convenient saving system which allows you to save at any time and rewind later if you want to make a different choice and/or change your course of direction. Though to get every possible outcome, you will probably need a lot more than just a few sets of savepoints. ..which I think is great and gives this game that much more replayability.
Whether you're a fan of Visual Novels, RPGs or otherwise.. I'd say it's definitely worth a buy.

I think they were onto something with this. The blue and red stages were very fun and enjoyable, and I wish they would have stuck with that concept and pushed it throughout the entire game.
Although at the time of writing this review, I only have a half hour on it, it was mostly because it stopped being fun and enjoyable once I got to the green section. It was fun, enjoyable, relaxing, that is until it kicked you in the face with the green part and was more frustrating than anything.
That's not to say there isn't a person that would love this game. Anybody that derives an enjoyment from hard puzzles should absolutely love this game. But I'll have to say, if you're interested because you just want to unwind on something simple and fun, you'll only enjoy the first ~20 minutes worth of this game. After that, it stops becoming relaxing and more mentally intensive.
If, in the future, they release another version of this game with just blue and maybe red sections of this game expanded upon further without throwing in the green and beyond, that is something that I would completely recommend.
For now, though, I'm torn on a recommendation. I can't simply say yes, and I can't simply say no. It's a game for a type of person. If you are that puzzley, determined person, then this is completely for you. If you're somebody that gets frustrated easily, this isn't for you.

If you are a fan of the 2D, side-scrolling adventure games, Starbound does provide a slight sense of space voyage with a hint of base building. The main story is overall lackluster, and the planets tend to get very repetitive. The main thing it does provide is mod support for some serious decoration for spaceship and homeworlds alike. I will not say Starbound is a bad game, a lot of potential is there, but it is a bad purchase for the current state of the game.

Pros: You rarely have a chance to be bored, and the interactions are great.
UI is easy enough to use with only a few things I'd fix on it's current functioning.
Gets you invested in several characters, leaving room for you to "lose" someone, yet still get to play since you -are- anyone you play.
The Juggernauts... lets just say you don't get used to them enough to not pee just a bit when they roar near you. Some of the realistic take-downs still make you cringe no matter how long you play (may be a con for some, but it's supposed to keep you cringing, well done here).
I enjoyed that the missions weren't all time sensitive, nor were all urgent to your gameplay. But still enough were to keep you on your toes.
Vehicles offered to choose from all varied in handling, speed and passenger capacity. Making it necessary for you to find the right vehicle for the right job at times.
Large enough map for the time-frame it takes to make this game happen.
Cons: I felt there was more that could have been done before ending as quickly as it did, though there wasn't any forced ending really, if you didn't know what was coming, you would just wind up with it ended. I suppose it had to get there some time. State of Decay Breakdown addresses this by giving you a choice as to when you want to boggie out however.
UI: needs a search function, or a filter when faced with finding characters in your group to choose from. At 40+ to choose from it's tougher to find who you need relatively quickly.
The tutorial could have been a tad more interactive. In-game tuts irritate me, but only if I've seen them already. So in-game tut plus a toggle wouldn't hurt. Though learning hands-on is doable.
Game function itself was great. Absolutely nothing mentioned in the "cons" was game breaking by any means. Well worth the price for what you get. Def a recommended play if you enjoy the jump-scares and immersive style games.

Undead Labs comes out with a fantastic twist on the Zombie genre. State of Decay introduces high level survival involving base establishment, building, resource management, questing, and zombie apocalypse all mixed together.
A simple fishing trip in Mt. Tanner goes completely wrong for our starting hero Marcus Campbell and his friend Ed Jones. It doesn’t take long for Trumbell Valley to go down the toilet as the zombie virus spreads throughout the land. With an abundance of cast it is up to whomever you decide to bring the remaining survivors together and figure out what the military is up to in this forsaken valley.
State of Decay is not like any other game you’ll play. Your characters are completely dynamic in that anyone who dies is lost forever, but the campaign continues as if the person lost never existed to begin with. The campaign is delivered through missions that are randomly assigned based on events on the map and total missions currently in progress. The missions vary from side-missions with a story, the main campaign, and then random filler missions. Although, be careful because the missions can also glitch if you develop too quickly resulting in the campaign never fully deploying. In my person campaign I was unable to actually beat it despite playing 30+ hours because my final missions never deployed as I had too many filler missions blocking the deployment of the final campaign missions.
Each person you find has independent experience sets which can be raised to make each character as strong as the last. Selecting from a list of customized traits combined with unique character traits you can fully develop unique characters. I found myself playing different characters just to level them so they would be more competent when running scavenger missions or hunt missions. The stronger you make each of your survivors the more competent they are in battle; sadly they do not level unless you play them. Some traits like wits and cardio are only applicable if you are using the survivor. On the other hand some traits like fighting and special unique traits transfer making them much more useful in combat.  The zombies you fight have various speeds which allow them to be each unique in how you much approach them, but not only are the regulars different they’ve also provided special zombies which include: SWAT, Bloater, Juggernaut, Screamer, and Feral. The SWAT is essentially a regular zombie with armor making them invulnerable to bullets; the bloater is a zombie that upon death releases toxic gas; the juggernaut is a very strong zombie that although in vulnerable to all attacks is not able to be knocked back; the screamer is a zombie that releases you guessed it a mighty scream that attracts other zombies and stuns survivors; finally the feral which the scariest of the lot uses its high speed to pin survivors (similar to a hunter), but with enough work you can get them off.
Breakdown:
I haven’t played Breakdown truly, but from the little I did it seems like just the regular game with less base management and more free-roam. The little objectives are made null and instead you focus on character development. I will update this once I figure out more about the game.
Lifeline:
This is probably one of the best DLC expansions I have ever seen. Lifeline offers a whole new city with new features that make a brilliant campaign. The city although not fully unlocked provides a campaign that can be finished in two ways with a score-card based on your progress through the campaign. For every thirty-forty minutes a siege occurs on your home base where you must hold up against an even greater foe. Each level there are more zombies, hordes, and even infestations. This progressively makes the campaign more difficult to play – of course at the same time each of the survivors becomes more powerful as you train them up. This campaign offers an interesting story with new dynamics and features.
State of Decay and its DLC’s are a brilliant set to add to the zombie genre. The permanent death feature is a great addition to the game by making each character the protagonist. This adds a huge amount of depth to the gameplay as well as the story. In fact the Lifeline DLC reminds me of how expansions traditionally used to be, a whole new game that built off the old one rather than just a single unlock. This is a fantastic zombie game with amazing combat, character dynamics, and story. Despite some glitches that may make the campaign unbeatable the game is still definitely a lot of fun. I would recommend this game and its DLCs especially if you can grab it on a sale.
Pros:
+Permanent death, which means every survivor is the protagonist.
+Base building; depending on your gameplay you can either go big or small. You get to play how you want the campaign to flow.
+Other survivor camps, they are spread throughout the game and appear randomly to make the world seem more alive.
+Character customization, each character although has the same attributes is unique based on how you play them.
+Fun combat system, lots of weapons and different play styles that combine with abilities.
Cons:
-The game may glitch causing you to be unable to complete the campaign.
-Lifeline has a spawn glitch, possibly due to the smaller playable area, where zombies spawn randomly even right within range as you are fighting. If you turn the camera and then immediately turn it back around the area will usually be full of zombies again.
